settings.introHTML:
This lesson teaches learners how to talk about university studies in French, including degree programmes, years of study, lectures, seminars, tutorials, and academic workload. It introduces useful expressions such as faire des études, faire une licence, faire un master, and avoir un emploi du temps chargé.

It also practises how to describe subjects, student life, essays, research, and the feelings that often go with study, such as being fatigué(e), occupé(e), or stressé(e).
settings.informationHTML:
After completing this unit, you will be able to:

  • Say what and where you study, and talk about degrees and years of study.
  • Use university vocabulary for lectures, seminars, research, essays, and academic life.
  • Ask more natural French questions with comme, especially about studies and preferences.
  • Use devoir and pouvoir with infinitives to talk about obligations and possibilities.
  • Recognise and use present and past participles as adjectives more accurately.

phrases: Qu'est-ce que tu fais comme études ?
No, I'm doing a bachelor's degree / I'm an undergrad.
Are you in the first year?
Non, je suis en deuxième année.
No, I'm in the second year
Moi, je fais une fac d'architecture. Je suis en première année de master.
I'm studying architecture. I'm in the first year of a masters.
Et ton copain ? Il étudie l'architecture aussi ?
What about your boyfriend? Is he studying architecture too?
Non, il est doctorant. Il fait un doctorat en langues médiévales. Il écrit sa thèse. Il est très occupé. Il passe des heures à la bibliothèque !
No, he's a PhD student. He's doing a PhD in medieval languages. He's writing his dissertation. He's very busy. He's spending hours at the library!
phraseTable1.informationTextHTML: Read each line, then play the audio to hear how speakers ask about degree subjects and levels of study.
Listen for the way the speakers ask what someone is studying, describe degree level, and talk about doctoral work.

phrases: Alice, ça va ? Tu as l'air très fatigué aujourd'hui !
Alice, are you alright? You look very tired today!
Non, ça ne va pas aujourd'hui ! Je suis très fatiguée.
No, I'm not alright today. I'm very tired.
Cette semaine j'ai cinq cours magistraux, deux séminaires et deux tutorats ! Et beaucoup de lecture !
This week I've got five lectures, two seminars and two tutorials. And lots of reading!
C'est vraiment beaucoup ! Tu as un emploi du temps très chargé, Alice !
That really is a lot! You've got a very heavy timetable, Alice!
Oui, et je dois écrire deux dissertations aussi ! C'est trop ! Je suis très stressée !
Yes, and I have to write two essays as well. It's too much! I'm very stressed!
Mais ça va aller, Alice ! C'est bientôt les vacances et tu peux te reposer !
But it'll be alright, Alice! It'll soon be the holidays, and you can have a rest!
phraseTable2.informationTextHTML: Read each line, then play the audio to hear how speakers describe workload, pressure, and reassurance.
Notice how the speakers describe a heavy timetable, essays, and feeling tired or stressed.

vocabulary.informationTextHTML: This section introduces the core university words and useful expressions used throughout the lesson.

You will learn:

  • Words for people and roles such as étudiant(e), doctorant(e), chercheur / chercheuse, and professeur.
  • Useful expressions for studies and degrees such as faire des études, licence, master, and doctorat.
  • Names of academic subjects, years of study, and teaching formats such as cours magistral, séminaire, and tutorat.
  • Adjectives and phrases used to describe workload and feelings, such as fatigant, stressant, and avoir un emploi du temps chargé.

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section explains how French uses comme in idiomatic questions, how devoir and pouvoir work with infinitives, and how present and past participles can be used as adjectives.

grammar1.informationTextHTML: In this part, focus on how comme helps French ask what kind of studies, music, sport, or food someone is talking about.

grammar2.informationTextHTML: Here, concentrate on how devoir changes with the subject and how it combines with another verb to express obligation.

grammar3.informationTextHTML: This part shows how pouvoir expresses ability or possibility and how its present-tense forms change.

grammar4.titleTextHTML: 4. Present and past participles as adjectives
grammar4.informationTextHTML: Focus on the difference between -ant forms such as intéressant and -é forms such as fatigué, and remember adjective agreement.

items.text: Je fais une fac [*d'|de|en|à|sur|avec] anthropologie. Je suis en troisième année [*de|en|d'|à|pour|avec] licence.
Et ta [*copine|doctorante|licence|thèse|bibliothèque|fac] ? Elle étudie l' [*anthropologie|politique|bibliothèque|année|histoire|licence] aussi ?

Non, elle est [*doctorante|copine|licence|master|tutrice|étudiante]. Elle fait un doctorat en histoire [*médiévale|politique|anglaise|française|première|universitaire]. Elle écrit sa [*thèse|licence|année|fac|politique|histoire]. Elle est très [*occupée|médiévale|anthropologie|première|doctorante|universitaire]. Elle passe des heures à la [*bibliothèque|politique|copine|thèse|licence|fac] !

instructionsLayout.paragraphHTML: This section gives you a chance to practise the key points from this unit. You will check your use of devoir and pouvoir with infinitives, ask everyday questions with comme, and recognise present and past participles used as adjectives — all in the context of talking about studies.
